summary: Frontend-only E2E testing of the static Bitcoin Kids landing page (RU). Verified page load, all data-testids, header/hero/program CTAs, week & FAQ accordions (10 + 7), lead form submission with toast + form reset, footer legal pages (200), image loading, and mobile burger menu toggle. All checks passed with zero console/page errors.
critical_code_review_comments: Tailwind CDN (cdn.tailwindcss.com) is used in production HTML — it emits a console warning and adds runtime cost. For production consider building Tailwind CSS with the CLI/PostCSS. Non-blocking.

Lead form is 100% client-side (main.js just shows a toast and resets). No lead is persisted or emailed — this is a real business gap for a 'selling landing'. Add a backend endpoint (e.g., POST /api/leads) or a Telegram/email webhook so leads are actually captured.
No honeypot / rate-limit / captcha on the lead form — if a backend is added later, spam risk should be considered.
footer-disclaimer is the only footer link with a data-testid; the other 4 legal links (privacy/offer/cookies/refunds) don't have testids. Cosmetic — not required by the review scope.
IntersectionObserver 'reveal' animation logic is fine but the page has ~30+ .reveal nodes; consider disconnecting the observer once all are revealed (minor perf).
form.reset() runs BEFORE the toast is shown — that's actually the desired UX here (form clears when success shows). Just noting the ordering is intentional and correct.
test_credentials: N/A — no auth in this app
context_for_next_testing_agent: Pure static site served by /app/frontend/server.mjs on port 3000. Preview URL responds at root. Everything tested via Playwright against the preview URL. Data-testids match the spec exactly: nav-{about,benefits,program,faq}, header-cta, hero-primary-cta, hero-secondary-cta, program-cta, week-item-1..10 / week-trigger-N, faq-item-1..7 / faq-trigger-N, lead-form, lead-name-input, lead-contact-input, lead-age-input, lead-submit, success-toast, burger-button, footer-disclaimer, hero-mascot-img, benefit-image, format-image. Lead form submits client-side only — no network call, no backend endpoint.
